name: security-clickhouse-row-policies-review
intent: ClickHouse effective row policies, roles and alternate data paths
artifacts: Users/roles, row policies, query settings, views/table functions and actual connection identity.
trace: Trace which policies apply to the selected table/query identity and whether a permitted alternate engine/view path bypasses the intended tenant restriction.
experiment: Use isolated synthetic tenant rows with an ordinary application identity; compare entitled query and one reachable alternate path.
disproof: A superuser seeing all rows or an unused table-function name is not an application-user bypass.
repair: Apply the intended policy to effective data paths and test legitimate analytics and foreign-row denial.
branch_decisions: Evaluate active roles and permissive/restrictive policy composition for the installed version and table operation. SELECT row policy is not a universal write or external-table guard. A user with unrestricted alternative access may intentionally bypass the filtered view; distinguish an application boundary from a privileged DBA role.
operational_method: Expand applicable roles and policy expressions: permissive policies combine as OR and restrictive policies constrain the result with AND. Resolve deployed-version/settings behavior when no policy applies, rather than assuming a universal default. Record the actual table operation and alternate view/table functions. Compare a mixed-tenant owned dataset under one role and the effective role set; SELECT filtering alone does not establish write or external-source confinement.
